{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABd2pK3g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHXruo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 255, "title": "Simplify Graph Library into a clean Graphs / Launch Settings sidebar layout (approved mockup)", "body": "## Goal

Implement the **approved visual mockup from the design discussion (2026-11-10)**: a calm, spacious, light-mode desktop UI with a **persistent left navigation sidebar**, a **Graph Library panel** in the main left column and a **Launch Settings panel** in the main right column. The previous #250 master/detail + #253 full-width bottom launch settings became visually complex. This task is a layout/visual hierarchy refinement, **not** a change to the graph/launch data model.

The approved image shows:
- narrow app navigation rail at far left: **Graphs** (active), **Launch Settings**, **Models**, **Settings**;
- a Graph Library card with header **Graph Library**, a prominent **+ New Graph** button and a short vertical list of graph cards;
- a Launch Settings card **beside** it, with two separate stacked settings cards: **Live Window** (graph picker) and **Web Page Microphone** (graph picker + independent ON/OFF toggle);
- white/off-white background, generous whitespace, restrained blue accent, subtle borders, modest corner radii, no dense tables or instructional walls of text.

### Reference mockup

The user-approved image is attached in the conversation, not automatically available as a repository asset. **Use the detailed specification below as the authoritative implementation brief**; do not block work if the image cannot be accessed by the implementer.

```text
┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│ [Graph icon] App │  Graph Library      [+ New]  │  Launch Settings             │
│                  │                              │                              │
│ [Graphs]         │  [Search graphs…] [⋯filter]  │  ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│ [Launch Settings]│                              │  │ Live Window            │  │
│ ───────────────  │  ┌────────────────────────┐  │  │ [Meeting Notes      ▾] │  │
│ [Models]         │  │ Voice Input         ⋯  │  │  └────────────────────────┘  │
│ [Settings]       │  │ speech to text          │  │                              │
│                  │  ├────────────────────────┤  │  ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│                  │  │ Meeting Notes       ⋯  │  │  │ Web Page Microphone ON│  │
│                  │  │ transcription/summary  │  │  │ [Voice Input        ▾]│  │
│                  │  ├────────────────────────┤  │  └────────────────────────┘  │
│                  │  │ Translation         ⋯  │  │                              │
│                  │  │ speech translation     │  │                              │
│                  │  ├────────────────────────┤  │                              │
│                  │  │ Voice Reply         ⋯  │  │                              │

└──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

Names/descriptions are **illustrative sample data**, not hard-coded graph records. No fake product data or settings in production.

## Required UI structure and behavior

### 1. Persistent, clear navigation

- Replace the crowded horizontal page navigation on this screen with a **slim left sidebar** using the app's actual navigation destinations. Show Graphs as current; include access to Launch Settings, Models and existing settings destinations **only if implemented**. Do not create dead links or invent a settings page. Use accessible icons + labels, not icons alone.
- The **Graphs** and **Launch Settings** sidebar entries should navigate/focus/scroll to their respective areas on this screen (or switch two in-page sections while preserving the approved desktop side-by-side presentation); avoid duplicating independent routes or creating two inconsistent copies of the settings. Make active/focus states obvious.
- Preserve working access to Live, Graph Editor, Models and existing app navigation. Don't accidentally make Live or Graph Editor inaccessible just to match the picture. Reuse existing navigation infrastructure where feasible.

### 2. Graph Library panel: browsing first, not a dense editor

- Main left card header: **Graph Library**, prominent **+ New Graph**.
- Display graphs as **compact, spacious selectable cards/rows** with name and optional *short* description, selected highlight, and a small **⋯ menu** for secondary actions. Do not render a five-column table, text-input-like list buttons, per-row technical status or assignment badges.
- Keep search, sort/filter, import, empty state, recovery and model cache access, but demote secondary controls (e.g. compact toolbar, More menu) so the list stays visually clean. Search/filter must remain discoverable and functional.
- **Graph selection and graph editing must remain accessible**. The mockup omits the old large selected-graph detail pane, but we must NOT silently delete its functionality:
  - Selecting a graph may open a **focused detail view, drawer, dialog or a clearly navigable detail subview** with graph preview, **Edit graph**, Duplicate, editable Name/Description + Save, Export JSON, Check model files, Delete and recovery info.
  - Prefer a detail subview/drawer that does not permanently create a *third* full-size column. Provide an obvious Back/Close and restore focus to the invoking graph row. Alternatively, a single-card detail view replacing the library list is acceptable on narrow screens.
  - Keep dirty-edit warnings, saved draft recovery, conflict checks, graph validation and deletion guards. Make menu actions discoverable and keyboard operable; no click-only hover controls.
- Graph list remains general-purpose: **no `Use this graph for` block or Live/Web-specific assignment markers**.

### 3. Launch Settings panel: alongside Graph Library

- On desktop, **Launch Settings is the main right panel**, not a full-width section below the graph editor/details. Its visual weight is comparable to the Graph Library panel, with a clean heading and minimal explanatory copy.
- Show exactly the current two launch entry points as **two visually separated settings cards**:
  - **Live Window**: choose a saved executable graph via dropdown.
  - **Web Page Microphone**: choose an eligible saved graph via dropdown, and independently switch website mic controls **ON/OFF**.
- Use simple, entry-point-oriented names. Avoid `Default execution targets`, `Use this graph for`, and overly prominent `Web voice typing` jargon. Do not tie the selected library graph to a launch assignment.
- Keep the selectors always readable, long names truncated accessibly, no redundant `Using: ...` prose when a dropdown already shows the selection. Web mic may be `Not assigned`; Live must have a valid graph.
- The toggle is **not** the graph selector. Choosing a graph never enables website injection. Switching OFF retains the assignment. Keep permission consent **just-in-time** on enabling, with existing native Chrome permissions, errors, and optional concise help. Keep accessible status/denial feedback; no permanent explanatory wall.
- Incompatible graphs must not become launchable (preserve `usable` and `webVoiceError` checks). Changing a binding affects only the next session; running sessions keep snapshots.

### 4. Visual design / responsive

- Use the mockup's **clean desktop visual hierarchy**: sidebar ~180–220px, remaining workspace two balanced cards, subtle borders/shadows, airy spacing, restrained blue highlights and clearly distinguished selected graph. Treat dimensions as guidance, not fixed pixel constraints.
- Respect existing app theme/accessibility (including dark mode or forced colors if supported); avoid broad, unrequested changes to Graph Editor or Live. Keep asset dependencies local (no remote fonts/icons).
- On narrow screens, collapse the sidebar into an accessible compact navigation and **stack the two main panels**; keep graph detail as a navigable subview. Avoid squeezed multi-column forms, clipped popovers or horizontal overflow.
- Avoid unnecessary nesting of boxes and repetitive microcopy. Preserve meaningful focus rings, labels, touch targets, ARIA and screen-reader status.

## Engineering constraints

- Implement in `extension/graph-library.html`, `extension/graph-library.css`, `extension/graph-library-page.js` and existing shared navigation/CSS as appropriate, plus tests/docs. Keep scope to this UI.
- Preserve `GraphLibrary` persistence and assignments `{ live, webVoice }`, stable IDs, revision/locking, multi-tab sync, import/export, graph selection, validation/recovery and model cache checks. **No schema or migration**.
- Preserve the Web voice ON/OFF preference in `chrome.storage.local`, explicit permission gating and website injection/recording lifecycle. Do not change ASR, runtime, or X/Twitter insertion behavior.
- Existing tests may use stable IDs such as `#graph-list`, `#live-graph`, `#web-graph`, `#web-voice-enabled`, `#voice-consent`, `#selected`, `#graph-name`, `#details-form`; preserve where practical or update selectors and tests together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Desktop screen visually matches the approved concept: **slim left sidebar + Graph Library panel left + Launch Settings panel right**. No bottom-wide launch block or permanently visible giant detail panel.
- [ ] Graph cards show name, short description and discoverable ⋯ action; clicking a card exposes complete graph management/preview/edit functionality in a focused, dismissible view.
- [ ] Graph browsing and launch configuration are clearly distinct; no `Use this graph for` in graph details and no use-specific markers in the list.
- [ ] Launch Settings has **Live Window** and **Web Page Microphone** rows/cards with independent graph selection and ON/OFF switch; assignments and permissions retain existing semantics.
- [ ] Existing search/sort/filter, import/export, rename/save, duplicate/delete, model cache inspection, dirty edits, recovery, validation, cross-tab revisions and permissions still work.
- [ ] Live and Graph Editor navigation still accessible; sidebar items do not lead to dead pages.
- [ ] Responsive mobile, keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, focus return, zoom and contrast remain usable.
- [ ] Update automated UI/browser tests and screenshots/docs where relevant; verify no behavioral regression and report tests actually executed.

## Related work

#250 introduced the master/detail UI; #253 separated launch configuration from graph management. This task refines **visual presentation** using the newly approved image, without undoing their underlying separation.
